chunks: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Imran al-Nakha'i, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Isma'il ibn Muslim. He said: Abu Nu'aym al-Balkhi narrated to us from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (may God's mercy be upon him).

He said: I was holding the hand of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and we were walking together. We did not stop gazing at the Sun until it set. So I said: O Messenger of God, where does it go? He said: Into the sky. Then it is raised from one heaven to another until it is raised to the highest seventh heaven, until it is beneath the Throne. It then falls in prostration, and the angels appointed over it prostrate along with it. Then it says: O Lord, from where do You command me to rise — from my setting point, or from my rising point?

That is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: 'The Sun runs to a resting place appointed for it; that is the design of the Almighty, the All-Knowing' (36:38) — meaning thereby the fashioning of the Mighty Lord in His dominion over His creation.

He said: Then Gabriel comes to it with a garment of radiance from the light of the Throne, proportioned to the hours of the day — long in summer, short in winter, or intermediate in autumn and spring. He said: Then it puts on that garment just as one of you puts on his clothes. Then it proceeds with it through the expanse of the sky until it rises from its rising point.
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: It is as though I see it having been detained for about three nights, then stripped of its radiance, and commanded to rise from its setting point.
That is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: 'When the Sun is rolled up, and when the stars fall' (81:1–2).

And the Moon is likewise — in its rise, its course along the horizon of the sky, its setting, and its ascent to the seventh heaven. It prostrates beneath the Throne, and Gabriel comes to it with a garment from the light of the Footstool.
That is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: 'He is the One who made the Sun a radiance and the Moon a light' (10:5).
Abu Dharr (may God's mercy be upon him) said: Then I withdrew with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and we prayed Maghrib.

key_terms.الْعَرْش: The Divine Throne (al-'Arsh) — the highest of God's created realms in Islamic cosmology
key_terms.الْكُرْسِيّ: The Footstool (al-Kursi) — beneath the Throne in rank, referenced in Ayat al-Kursi (2:255)
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَة الْمُوَكَّلُون: The appointed angels — angels specifically assigned to oversee the Sun's journey
key_terms.حُلَّة ضَوْء: A garment of radiance — the luminous vestment bestowed upon celestial bodies
key_terms.سَاجِدَة: Prostrating (sajidah) — the Sun's act of submission to God at the Throne

ai.seo_question: Where does the Sun go after it sets according to hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by the eminent Companion Abu Dharr al-Ghifari from the Prophet (SAWW), presents a cosmological vision of the celestial mechanics of the Sun and Moon as understood in prophetic teaching. The Sun, after setting, ascends through the seven heavens, prostrates beneath the Divine Throne, and awaits God's command before rising again — a nightly act of submission witnessed by appointed angels. Three Quranic verses (36:38, 81:1-2, 10:5) are cited to confirm this cosmological framework, with the hadith interpreted as the deeper meaning behind the Quran's description of the Sun's 'appointed course.' The Moon follows an identical pattern, receiving a garment of light from the Footstool (Kursi) rather than the Throne — a detail distinguishing the rank of the two celestial bodies.

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Musa b al-Mutawakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us from Musa b. `Imran al-Nakha`I from his uncle al-Husayn b. Yazid from Isma`il b. Muslim. He said: Abu Na`im al-Balkhi narrated to us from Muqatil b. Hayyan from `Abd al-Rahman b. Abza from Abi Dharr al-Ghifari (rh).

He said: I was holding the hand of the Messenger of Allah (s) and we were walking together. We did not stop looking to the Sun until it set. So, I said: O Messenger of Allah! Where does it go? He said: In the sky. Then, it rises from heaven to heaven until it reaches the highest, seventh heaven; till it is beneath the Throne. It then falls in prostration, and the angels of the kingdom of heaven prostrate with it. Then, it says: “O Lord! Where do You order me to rise from: from my setting place, or from my rising place?”
That is His saying, “The Sun travels for a fixed term. That is the design of the Almighty, the Knowing” [36:38] – meaning, that is the contrivance of the Mighty Lord in His kingdom with His creation.

He said: So, Gabriel (as) comes to it with a garment which glows with the light of the Throne, which is in accordance with the hours of the day – it lengthens in the summer, it shortens in the winter, and it is in between that in the fall and the spring. He said: Then, it wears that garment just as one of you wears his clothes. Then, it goes with it in the sky until it rises from its rising point.
The Prophet (s) said: It is as though I am with it as it is confined for three nights, and it is not cloaked in [its] glow, and it is ordered to rise from its setting place.
That is His saying, “When the Sun is turned, and when the stars darken” (81:1-2).

The Moon is like that from its rise, to its journey to the horizon of the sky, to its setting, to its ascension to the seventh heaven. It prostrates beneath the Throne, and Gabriel (as) comes to it with a garment of the light of the Seat.
That is His saying, “He is the one that made the Sun a shining glow and the Moon a light.” [10:5]
Abu Dharr (rh) said: Then, I withdrew with the Messenger of Allah (s) and we prayed Maghrib.
